summary.text: Crystal twinning is when two or more neighbouring crystals of the same mineral share some lattice points in a symmetrical way, forming a tightly bonded intergrowth.
Twins follow twin laws specific to the crystal structure, so the type of twinning can help identify a mineral.
Twinning can arise during growth, during a change in crystal structure, or in response to shear stress.

items.prompt: A rock holds a twinned pair of crystals and, nearby, two grains that touch at random angles. Which junction is harder to pull apart?

options.label: The randomly touching grains, which interlock
Both are equally strong
Neither holds; both fall apart easily
The twins, because they share lattice points

items.explain: Shared lattice points make the junction between twin segments much stronger than that between randomly oriented grains.

items.prompt: A cluster of aligned crystals turns out to have one continuous lattice running all the way through. Is it twinned?

options.label: No, it is really one single crystal
Yes, aligned crystals are always twins
Yes, a deformation twin
No, it is a random polycrystal

items.explain: This is parallel growth: the cluster is actually a single crystal, and since its lattice is continuous it is not twinning.

items.prompt: Why can the way a crystal is twinned help a geologist tell which mineral it is?

options.label: Twins form only in one rare mineral
Twin laws are as typical of a mineral as its face angles
Twinned crystals are always larger
Twinning changes the mineral's chemistry

items.explain: Twin laws are as characteristic of a mineral as its crystal face angles, so the type of twinning is a diagnostic tool.

items.prompt: A crystal is put under shear stress and twins develop as it permanently changes shape. Which kind of twinning is this?

options.label: Growth twinning
Transformation twinning
Deformation twinning
Parallel growth

items.explain: Deformation twinning develops in response to shear stress and is an important mechanism for permanent shape changes in a crystal.

items.prompt: A reflection relates the two halves of a twinned crystal. Is that same reflection a symmetry of the untwinned single crystal?

options.label: Yes, every twin plane is a mirror of the crystal
Only in crystals of the cubic system
No, it is not among its normal symmetries
Only when both halves are equal in size

items.explain: The twin operation is not one of the normal symmetry operations of the untwinned crystal, for example a reflection across a plane that is not one of its symmetry planes.

items.prompt: Two crystal segments meet along one flat boundary and look like mirror images across it. What kind of twin is this?

options.label: A penetration twin
A contact twin
A parallel growth
A random intergrowth

items.explain: Contact twins meet on a single composition plane and often appear as mirror images across the boundary.
